//: dashboard/dashboard.config.example.json -- copy to dashboard.config.json and edit.
//1: DOCS ONLY: the service never auto-loads a *.example.json file.
//2: Precedence PER KEY: CLI flag > RC_DASH_* env var > this file > built-in default.
//3: Omitted keys fall back to a built-in default that PROBES a candidate list.
//4: Run `uv run python -m rc_dashboard --print-config` to see what each key
//5: actually resolved to and why, and `--check-feeds` to see what is on disk.
//6: Every '//'-prefixed key is stripped by the loader, so comments are legal here.

feeds.//1: as log/ebpfm/<date>/<host>.jsonl -- the log/ebpfm symlink already ends in /logs.
feeds.//2: List every root to merge; a non-existent root is reported, never fatal.

ebpf.//x: days must COVER live.retention_min, or the far end of the widest
ebpf.//y: window reads as a gap: 8 = 7 days of retention + one, because hosts
ebpf.//z: roll over independently and the oldest day is still being written.
ebpf.//3: max_age_s: residency_totals is written UNCONDITIONALLY every
ebpf.//4: EBPFM_RESIDENCY_S (default 60s) whether or not anything was tracked,
ebpf.//5: so freshness here means liveness, not activity. 300 = 5 ticks, the same

feeds.//7: Node tier (unprivileged): node_snapshot.py is a vendored copy of
feeds.//8: collect/common/snapshot.py, so log/login is schema-compatible and works
feeds.//9: as a stand-in before `ebpfm --node` is deployed anywhere.

ebpf_node.//10: 2 snapshots: per_user_cgroup.cpu_usage_usec is CUMULATIVE, so a per-user
ebpf_node.//11: CPU rate only exists as a delta between two consecutive snapshots.

feeds.//12: collect/slurm_query.bash writes ONE FILE PER DAY into DEST_DIR, named
feeds.//13: SlurmData_<start>_<stop>-orig.csv. Point `dir` at DEST_DIR, not at a file.
feeds.//14: NOTE: sacct -D --starttime/--endtime overlap at midnight, so a job spanning
feeds.//15: two days appears in BOTH day-files; the reducer dedups on JobID.

//16: RETENTION vs WINDOW. retention_min is what the process HOLDS and the
//17: ceiling the page's picker can reach; window_min is only the view a fresh
//18: page opens on. Any window up to retention is an exact slice of the same
//19: per-minute BUCKETS -- never buffered raw events, which are ~10-20 GB/day
//20: fleet-wide. Raising window_min is free; raising retention_min costs
//21: memory (one slot per minute) and a longer startup backfill.

live.//22: Offered in the picker. Anything above retention_min is DROPPED from
live.//23: the list rather than offered and then silently clamped.
live.//24: backfill_hours: 0 starts empty and fills forward, skipping the one
live.//25: expensive startup read. Progress is exposed on /api/feeds.
live.//26: backfill_mb bounds that read PER FILE. The buckets discard anything
live.//27: older than retention on arrival, so over-reading costs time, never
live.//28: correctness; under-reading shows as a gap in the oldest bins, and
live.//29: /api/live reports `retained_from` so the page can say which.

//30: The historical reducers (quantiles, CCDFs, Gini, the dedup index) hold
//31: no time index and are not resumable from a byte offset, so a window
//32: change REBUILDS them from the rows -- seeking past everything older, so
//33: the cost is the window and not the day.

panels.//34: How many built windows to keep. Each costs reducer state, not just a
panels.//35: payload; 2 lets a reader compare a narrow and a wide view.
panels.//36: A built window keeps ingesting, so it drifts past its own span. It
panels.//37: re-scans once drift reaches this share of the window -- proportional,
panels.//38: so 1h refreshes often and cheaply and 7d rarely and expensively. The
panels.//39: drift is published either way; it is never rounded away.

trajectories.//2: idle_evict_s never reaches INSIDE the selected window -- the real
trajectories.//3: cutoff is max(idle_evict_s, window). Otherwise the panel would rank
trajectories.//4: 'sessions active in the last 2h' while labelling itself 24h.
trajectories.//5: max_sessions is therefore the memory bound, and it applies PER held
trajectories.//6: window: lower it if you raise live.retention_min on a busy fleet.
trajectories.//: 'usr' is excluded: a usr-keyed group is 'everything that user did',
trajectories.//1: which is not a trajectory. It is counted in by_key_type, never ranked.
